sentences.text: Heard Mr. H.R.A.Choudhury, learned Senior Counsel assisted by H.Ali, learned counsel for the Page No.# 2/3 petitioner as well as Mr. R.J.Baruah, learned Addl. P.P., Assam for the State respondent No.1.
Also heard Mr. R.Hoque, learned counse for respondent No.2.

This is an application filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C., by the petitioner, Shamsun Nahar praying for bail in connection with Kalgachia PS case No. 36/2024 under Sections 366/376(1)/313/417/34 IPC r/w Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a ward girl in the Barpeta Civil Hospital since 2013, working as a Grave-IV employee.
It is further submitted that Sections 376/366 IPC or Section 6 of POCSO Act is not attracted against the present petitioner.
It is further submitted that petitioner is in judicial custody for last 49 days, and considering length of detention, petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
The learned Addl.P.P. has produced the case diary and submits that the petitioner has accompanied the victim girl to one Rokiya Khatun who is the in-charge of Operation theatre in the hospital.
The said Rokiya Khatun has prescribed the medicine for terminating the pregnancy of the victim girl.
The learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 has submitted that he has no objection if the petitioner is granted bail.
I have perused the case diary including the statement of the victim girl recorded under section 164 CrPC wherein she had stated that due to physical relationship with one Faruk, she became pregnant.
Her pregnancy was terminated against her will at Kalgachia hospital and the accused family have paid Rs.10,000/- to the nurse.
One of the nurse is the petitioner.
However, it appears that the petitioner is not a nurse but she is a Grade -IV employee in the hospital.
It transpires that the petitioner was present at the time of terminating the pregnancy of the victim.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties as well as perusal of case diary and considering the length of detention, this Court is of the opinion that further custodial interrogation of the petitioner in the interest of investigation is not warranted.
